head: iOS 27 Connectivity Assist: iPhone uses cellular when Wi-Fi is weak
dek: iOS 27 has a switch called Connectivity Assist that lets your iPhone use cellular data when the Wi-Fi it's connected to is slow or unusable. You find it in Settings, Wi-Fi.
details: Apple's support page names places like the backyard, the driveway, coffee shops, airports and sports venues, where Wi-Fi is often there but too weak. It isn't used while the iPhone is roaming abroad, in cellular Low Data Mode, or with some third-party apps that stream audio and video. You can turn it off for one network to always stay on that Wi-Fi. With it on, the phone may use more cellular data.
means: If pages stall when you're at the edge of your Wi-Fi, the phone can now fall back to mobile data by itself. On a small data plan, that can eat into your allowance.
todo: Open Settings, tap Wi-Fi and scroll down to Connectivity Assist to switch it on or off; turn it off for a single network if you always want to stay on that Wi-Fi. Keep an eye on your data use in Settings or your carrier's app.
